title: Reza Tij Arrested by Security Forces in Badreh
content:
According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, Reza Tij was arrested on October 21, 2026, by plainclothes security agents.

According to the report, security forces entered his family home in the village of Pakal Garab, located in Badreh County, without presenting a judicial warrant. They arrested him and transferred him to an undisclosed location.

Despite his family’s efforts to obtain information, his fate and whereabouts remain unknown.

At the time of this report, no information was available regarding the reasons for his arrest or the charges brought against him.

Tij, 23, had previously been arrested on January 24, 2026, during the protests that took place in January of that year. He was temporarily released after some time.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, Reza Tij was arrested on October 21, 2026, by plainclothes security agents.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: 17-Year-Old Teenager Mohammad Lotfi Arrested by Security Forces in Baneh
content:
According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, Mohammad Lotfi, a 17-year-old teenager, was arrested. Security forces reportedly arrested the teenager at his workplace in Baneh on Tuesday, October 20, without presenting a judicial warrant.

Efforts by Mohammad Lotfi’s family to obtain information about his current situation through judicial authorities have so far been unsuccessful.

At the time of this report, no information was available regarding the reasons for his arrest, his whereabouts, or the charges brought against him.

title: Mohammad Azizi Remains in Detention and Legal Limbo at Choobindar Prison in Qazvin
content:
According to HRANA, Mohammad Azizi remains in detention.

A source close to his family confirmed the news to HRANA, stating: “Despite the passage of 30 days since Mr. Azizi’s arrest, he remains in legal limbo at Choobindar Prison in Qazvin. Some time ago, he was formally charged with propaganda against the regime on social media, disrupting public order and peace, insulting the Supreme Leader, and insulting religious sanctities.”

According to the source, despite his family’s efforts to secure his temporary release on bail, they have so far been unsuccessful.

On Wednesday, September 23, IRGC Intelligence agents arrested Mohammad Azizi at his residence in Alvand and transferred him to Choobindar Prison in Qazvin.

At the time of this report, no information was available regarding the specific actions underlying the charges against him.

Mohammad Azizi, a resident of Alvand, has previously faced arrest and judicial proceedings in connection with his activities.
snippet: According to HRANA, Mohammad Azizi remains in detention.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Omid and Chamran Ahmadinejad Arrested by IRGC Intelligence Agents in Ahvaz
content:
According to HRANA, Omid and Chamran Ahmadinejad, two residents of Ahvaz, were arrested.

Based on information obtained by HRANA, the two cousins were arrested by IRGC Intelligence agents in the early hours of Wednesday, October 21, and transferred to one of the agency’s detention facilities in Ahvaz.

A source close to the families confirmed the arrests to HRANA, stating: “Chamran Ahmadinejad was arrested at his home. Omid Ahmadinejad, who worked at a foam manufacturing workshop owned by Chamran and also lived on the premises, was arrested at the workshop.”

The source added that agents simultaneously searched the men’s residences and confiscated several personal belongings, including a workplace computer, laptops, and mobile phones.

According to information received by HRANA, despite follow-up efforts by the families, the relevant authorities have yet to provide a clear explanation regarding the reasons for the arrests or the charges brought against the two men.

Chamran Ahmadinejad, 30, married, and his cousin Omid Ahmadinejad, 36, are originally from Bahmai County and reside in Ahvaz.
snippet: According to HRANA, Omid and Chamran Ahmadinejad, two residents of Ahvaz, were arrested.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Ali Alipour, Father of Executed Political Prisoner, Arrested
content:
According to HRANA, Ali Alipour was arrested in Rasht. A source close to the family confirmed the arrest to HRANA, stating: “At 8:00 AM on Tuesday, October 20, security forces arrested Mr. Alipour at his residence and transferred him to the Shohadaye Gomnam detention facility in Rasht.”

The source added that, during the arrest, agents also confiscated several electronic devices belonging to Alipour and his family members.

At the time of this report, no information had been obtained regarding the reasons for Alipour’s arrest or the charges brought against him.

Ali Alipour is the father of Babak Alipour, a political prisoner who was executed on March 31 of this year at Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj.

It is worth noting that Rouzbeh Alipour, another son of Ali Alipour, was also arrested in February of last year and remains in a state of legal uncertainty at the Greater Tehran Prison.

title: Two Prisoners Executed in Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj
content:
According to HRANA, two prisoners were executed in Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj.

HRANA has confirmed the identity of one of the prisoners executed at dawn today, Wednesday, October 21, as Ahmad (last name unknown). The identity of the second prisoner remains under investigation.

According to information obtained by HRANA, the two prisoners had previously been arrested on murder charges in separate cases and subsequently sentenced to death by criminal courts.

At the time of this report, the executions of these two prisoners had not been officially announced by prison authorities or other relevant institutions.

Between October 10, 2025, and October 8, 2026, HRANA documented at least 2,003 executions across Iran, based on 1,857 reports, representing an increase of approximately 29% compared to the previous reporting period. During the same period, HRANA also documented 230 death sentences. For more detailed statistics and analysis of executions in Iran, read HRANA’s latest comprehensive report.
snippet: According to HRANA, two prisoners were executed in Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: January 2026 Protests: Ilya Ben-Rashid Sentenced to Death
content:
According to HRANA, Ilya Ben-Rashid, one of those arrested during the January 2026 protests and currently held in Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan, has been sentenced to death, imprisonment, and additional punishments.

The verdict was issued by Branch 5 of the Isfahan Revolutionary Court and communicated to Ben-Rashid yesterday. Under the ruling, he was sentenced to death on the charge of moharebeh (waging war against God) through participation in the destruction of public property.

The same court also sentenced him to three years, six months, and one day of discretionary imprisonment on the charge of assembly and collusion to commit crimes against national security, and nine months and one day in prison on the charge of propaganda against the regime, with time already served in detention credited toward his sentence.

Additionally, as a supplementary punishment, he was sentenced to a two-year travel ban prohibiting him from leaving the country.

In April of this year, a hearing on the charges against Ben-Rashid was held before the same branch of the court.

title: Supreme Court Upholds Manouchehr Fallah’s Death Sentence Again
content:
According to HRANA, citing Emtedad, the Supreme Court has upheld the death sentence issued against Manouchehr Fallah.

Fallah’s death sentence, which was reissued in June 2026 by Branch 1 of the Rasht Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Ahmad Darvish Goftar, has been upheld by the Supreme Court. According to the report, the political prisoner’s case has been referred to the Criminal Sentence Enforcement Unit in Rasht for implementation of the sentence.

In February 2025, Manouchehr Fallah was sentenced to death by Branch 2 of the Rasht Revolutionary Court on the charge of moharebeh (enmity against God). The sentence was reportedly upheld by the Supreme Court in November of the same year. However, following the acceptance of a request for retrial, the Supreme Court overturned the ruling and referred the case to Branch 1 of the Rasht Revolutionary Court for reconsideration.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Emtedad, the Supreme Court has upheld the death sentence issued against Manouchehr Fallah.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Prisoner Executed in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad
content:
According to HRANA, citing Haal Vsh, a prisoner was executed in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad.

The prisoner has been identified as Abdullah Narouei (Hashem Shavabzahi), approximately 43 years old, the father of five children. He was originally from Zahedan and resided in Mashhad.

According to the report, Abdullah Narouei was arrested by security forces at his home in Mashhad on November 3, 2023. He was subsequently sentenced to death by the Revolutionary Court of Mashhad in January 2026 on drug-related charges.

On Monday, October 19, 2026, Narouei was transferred to the quarantine ward of Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. At dawn on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, he was executed by hanging at the prison without being granted a final visit with his family.

As of the time of this report, the execution has not been officially announced by prison authorities or other relevant institutions.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Haal Vsh, a prisoner was executed in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Political Prisoner Kazem Alinejad Remains on Hunger Strike Amid Denial of Medical Care
content:
According to HRANA, Kazem Alinejad, a political prisoner held in Evin Prison, is now on the fifth day of his hunger strike.

Alinejad began his hunger strike on Friday, October 16, 2026, in protest against the denial of medical services, lack of access to necessary medications, and prison authorities’ disregard for his physical health. Five days after the strike began, his demands for medical care remain unmet, and he continues his hunger strike.

The political prisoner suffers from heart, lung, and kidney conditions, as well as diabetes and high blood pressure. Despite these serious health issues, he has been denied access to some of his essential medications. His insulin intake has also increased due to elevated blood sugar levels, while his repeated requests to be transferred to medical facilities outside the prison have gone unanswered.
snippet: According to HRANA, Kazem Alinejad, a political prisoner held in Evin Prison, is now on the fifth day of his hunger strike.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Two Prisoners Executed in Mashhad Prison
content:
According to HRANA, citing Haal Vsh, two prisoners were executed in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad on Tuesday, October 20, 2026.

The prisoners have been identified as Abdollah Narouei (Hashem Shavabzehi), approximately 43 years old, a father of five, originally from Zahedan and residing in Mashhad, and Issa Narouei (Lakzehi), 30 years old, son of Osman, unmarried, originally from Zahedan and residing in Mashhad.

According to the report, Abdollah Narouei was arrested by security forces at his home in Mashhad on November 3, 2023. He was subsequently sentenced to death by the Revolutionary Court of Mashhad in December 2025–January 2026 on drug-related charges. His execution was carried out without allowing him a final visit with his family.

Issa Narouei was also arrested by security forces at his home in Mashhad in 2025–2026. He was subsequently sentenced to death by the Revolutionary Court of Mashhad on drug-related charges.

As of the time of this report, the executions of these prisoners have not been officially announced by prison authorities or the relevant institutions.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Haal Vsh, two prisoners were executed in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad on Tuesday, October 20, 2026.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Denied Medical Care: A Report on the Latest Situation of Teacher Hadi Jalali in Jiroft Prison
content:
According to HRANA, Hadi Jalali remains deprived of access to his medications and appropriate medical treatment.

An informed source close to Jalali’s family told HRANA: “Mr. Jalali, who is serving his prison sentence in Jiroft Prison, has been denied access to his medications despite suffering from mental health conditions.”

The source added: “He is being held in a ward designated for prisoners convicted of ordinary criminal offenses, in violation of the principle of separation of prisoners based on the nature of their offenses. He is also forced to sleep on the floor due to the lack of a bed and has been deprived of basic prison facilities.”

Jalali was transferred to Jiroft Prison in August 2026 to begin serving his prison sentence.

On June 9, 2026, Branch 7 of the Kerman Province Court of Appeals upheld the teacher’s conviction in full. He had previously been sentenced by the lower court to two years and seven months in prison on the charge of “disrupting national security.” His trial was held on February 11, 2025, before Branch 1 of the Revolutionary Court in Kerman.
snippet: According to HRANA, Hadi Jalali remains deprived of access to his medications and appropriate medical treatment.
